title: ADAEZE AND THE EMPTY CHAIR
deck: A dam must start before the rains, and the people it will bury have no vote. Adaeze chairs the hearing; Illuminara has twelve days to find the line between what cannot wait and what cannot be undone.
shape: Six scenes across twelve days: a hearing with an empty chair, a refusal between mother and daughter, a night spent breaking one schedule into three columns, a vote taken across three countries, an early storm in a dam gallery, and a seat that is no longer empty.

scenes.title: Item Zero
paragraphs: *Harrow Gorge Hearing Hall · Day One, 09:10*
The chair at the foot of the table was empty on purpose. Ash frame, rush seat, no nameplate. Adaeze had it carried in before the doors opened, and the clerk had entered it in the record as Item Zero.

Seven villages had stood below the old dam until the evacuation order eleven years ago. The order had also dissolved them. Their land was struck from the register, their councils with it, and under Rule Four only communities that occupied mapped ground could vote on the dam that would now be built over their graves.

**Halvard Roos**  
The left abutment gallery is seeping at two point two litres a second. My trigger is six. I will not tell this room the old dam is safe, and I will not tell it the new one can wait for a better hearing.

**Bukola Ferreira**  
Six hundred thousand people drink from this river and the rains come in nineteen days. Every hour spent on ghosts is an hour taken from them.
Adaeze did not look up from her papers. She had chaired basin hearings for twenty years, and she had learned that the quickest way to lose a room was to answer its first insult.

**Adaeze**  
The ghosts have names, Councillor. The clerk will read them at the end of every session until the rule changes. Witness Four, you may begin.

Illuminara had sat at the side table for an hour and no one had addressed her as anything else. That was the arrangement. Her mother had made it in the car, in four sentences, and had not asked whether it suited her.

**Illuminara**  
There are two workable routes for the spillway outfall. The right-bank route is straighter and cheaper, and it carries the outfall and the final spoil dump across the Pell terraces. The left-bank route takes three hundred and ten hectares of irrigated farmland in the Weir Valley and costs nine percent more. Both are safe. Neither is harmless.

**Halvard Roos**  
The contractor says the route must be fixed today. Haul road, spoil and cofferdam are one chain.

**Illuminara**  
That is what the schedule says. I have not yet checked whether it is what the rock says.
Beside the long table the empty chair held the window light. Nobody sat in it. Nobody looked at it either, which was how she knew they had all been counting it.

scenes.title: Rule Four
paragraphs: *Chair's office, Harrow Gorge Hearing Hall · Day One, 12:40*
Adaeze shut the door and took off her glasses, the only sign she gave of how the morning had gone.

**Illuminara**  
I have read all four thousand petitions, from three countries. I can model what each village would choose within a few percent and lodge it as a sealed finding. Then the chair is not empty.

**Adaeze**  
Say the second part again, slowly.

**Illuminara**  
I would not vote for them. I would tell the hearing what they would most probably say.

**Adaeze**  
Nara.
She said it as she had said it when her daughter was twenty-four and new to the courts: not a rebuke, a hand laid flat on a table.

**Adaeze**  
You taught me the first rule of your old trade. The interpreter carries what the speaker says. She does not improve it, and she does not supply it when the speaker is absent.

**Illuminara**  
They are not absent by choice.

**Adaeze**  
That is why it is not yours to supply. You would be the third body to decide for them, and kind about it this time. I have buried that kind of kindness.
*She is right. The model would be accurate, and it would still be a theft.*

**Illuminara**  
Then what do you want from me?

**Adaeze**  
The chair holds a veto and no vote. It can stop what cannot be undone and it cannot start anything. It stays empty until the burial societies choose witnesses to sit in it, and they will need twelve days, because they live in three countries and trust nobody. The room will ask me what those twelve days cost. I need you to tell me. Not what the villages want. Which decisions on that dam are still open if we wait, and which close for ever.

**Illuminara**  
That is an engineering question.

**Adaeze**  
It is the only kind I can take to Councillor Ferreira.
She had walked into the building to offer her mother an answer. She walked out holding a question, and it was the better of the two.

scenes.title: The Chain
paragraphs: *Contractor's site office, Harrow Gorge · Day One, 23:50*
Ruta Kasprzak's schedule ran to four hundred and twelve activities; Illuminara read them by ten. She had been asking which tasks were urgent. Adaeze had asked which could be undone.

She tagged each line with three questions. Does this move rock? Bury ground? Build something that must stand on the final choice? Thirty-one activities survived the third question. Nine touched either route. The rest formed one chain because it was cheapest to haul.

**Ruta Kasprzak**  
Line one hundred and eighty-four. Batching-plant pad. You put it in the middle column, reversible at a price.

**Illuminara**  
The slab can be broken out.

**Ruta Kasprzak**  
The forty anchor piles cross the right-bank haul alignment. Break the slab and the piles remain under whichever road loses. Pull them and I lose two days and nine hundred thousand.
Illuminara moved the row into the third column. The nine became ten.

**Illuminara**  
Then no piles until the route is chosen. Put the mobile plant on ballast. Add two days to concrete production and the nine hundred thousand to the hearing ledger.

**Ruta Kasprzak**  
You concede quickly for someone who read all four hundred and twelve.

**Illuminara**  
The ledger is useful only if the person who finds me wrong can change it.
Ruta tapped the column heading with one blunt fingernail. Illuminara added a blank beside every classification: challenger, evidence, time filed. No one had asked her for that column.

**Ruta Kasprzak**  
You are still asking me to double-handle the spoil.

**Illuminara**  
The first two hundred and sixty-two thousand cubic metres must come out before the rains whichever route wins. The cofferdam, diversion portal and abutment bolting touch neither the terraces nor the farmland. Only the final dump and the haul road across the terraces do. Send the rock to the old quarry bench instead, and nothing is buried that cannot be dug up again.

**Ruta Kasprzak**  
The bench holds three hundred thousand on the March survey. We've been blasting beside it since.

**Illuminara**  
Then we resurvey at dawn.
Halvard Roos came in at midnight with a flask and no intention of agreeing.

**Halvard Roos**  
You want a delay in my safety case for a legal fiction.

**Illuminara**  
I want a cost in it, not a delay. The temporary haul along the quarry track is slower: nine days of overtime, one point nine million, eleven days of the contractor's float. I have not found a cheaper way, and I am not claiming it is free.

**Halvard Roos**  
And if the rains come early? I have a gallery and a trigger. You have a spreadsheet.

**Illuminara**  
If the gallery crosses your trigger I can carry the shear on the left abutment for about thirty hours. Not twelve days. Thirty hours, and then I fail. The drawdown must do the rest: three point one metres starting tomorrow, which means the city's water is rationed from tomorrow.

**Halvard Roos**  
Then you are not in my safety case.

**Illuminara**  
I did not ask to be. Log it separately.

At dawn the resurvey came back at two hundred and eighty-nine thousand cubic metres, leaving twenty-seven thousand above the excavation target, three thousand short of Halvard's minimum reserve. Ruta leased a rail-yard stockpile for the final three thousand at a further hundred and eighty thousand. Halvard read both numbers twice and wrote them into the log in his own hand.

scenes.title: Three Countries
paragraphs: *Harrow Gorge Hearing Hall, three video links · Day Two, 10:00*

The links came up: a church hall in Corvane, a school gym in Tessaly, a shipping office in Lisk. For eleven years their burial societies had kept the seven villages' registers and sent money home for funerals when there was no home to return to.
Adaeze read the motion: an empty chair, a veto over irreversible work, no affirmative vote, a twelve-day interval and Illuminara's line-by-line ledger.

**Bukola Ferreira**  
This hands strangers a veto over my constituents' water. Whose water do these witnesses drink?

**Adaeze**  
Not yours. The veto touches only the third column. Rationing, the cofferdam and the foundation proceed.

**Mirela Haddad, from Corvane**  
And who owns the third column? Witness Four? Your safety authority?
Illuminara turned the ledger so all three cameras could see the blank beside every row.

**Illuminara**  
The safety authority classifies first. The chair's engineer may contest a row within twenty-four hours. The more irreversible reading governs until a reasoned ruling. Ruta found the row that proved the challenge belongs.

**Mirela Haddad, from Corvane**  
Then our engineer, paid by the hearing, reads your numbers and surveys the bench.

**Halvard Roos**  
If the gallery reaches its trigger while a row is disputed, protective work cannot wait.

**Illuminara**  
Only the work necessary to take the reading below the trigger, logged by the hour and reviewed the next day. The exception cannot choose a route.

**Savitri Moyo, from the Weir Valley**  
Same terms for us. Nobody here accepts the left bank for the valley. We meet on Day Eleven; record the dissent.

**Bukola Ferreira**  
Return the rule's operation to public hearing after one year. I can defend bounded delay, not invent a valley choice.

**Adaeze**  
Put both conditions in the motion.

**Mirela Haddad, from Corvane**  
Witness Four. Which route buries the Pell terraces?

**Illuminara**  
The right-bank route covers the lower three Pell terraces. I would choose the left for that reason, but it takes this hearing's farmland. I do not weigh those losses.

**Bukola Ferreira**  
My vote is yes, with the one-year review. The valley's vote remains its own.
The tally closed six to three. Rule Four took effect at noon. Adaeze, who did not vote, put her authorship and any blame into the record.

scenes.title: Thirty Hours
paragraphs: *Left abutment gallery, old Harrow Gorge dam · Day Eleven, 02:40*

The storm came nine days early: a hundred and forty millimetres in nine hours. The drawdown had bought three metres of freeboard and cost the city eleven days of rationing, but the sudden rise drove reservoir pressure through the known joint in the left abutment faster than the drains could clear it. Of the two hundred and sixty-two thousand cubic metres due out before the expected rains, two hundred and forty-seven thousand lay on the quarry bench. The remaining fifteen thousand was still rock in the river-side cut; the storm had arrived before its excavation shift.
At 02:40 the gallery drain read six point one litres a second.

**Halvard Roos, over the radio**  
It's crossed. Illuminara. Now.

She went in as far as the third joint. The concrete sweated cold. She laid both palms on the wall, found the plane along which the abutment wanted to slide, and began to carry what the rock had stopped carrying. It was not like lifting. It was like standing in a river that wished her to step aside.
She had told him thirty hours. She did not look at the clock.

**Halvard Roos, over the radio**  
Five point four. Falling. Keep going.
*Not for ever. Only until the drawdown is the stronger thing.*

At hour nineteen the reservoir inflow passed its crest. With the rain already gone and the reservoir three metres lower than it would otherwise have been, the drains took the load back. The reading fell to two point nine and held there. Halvard came down the gallery himself, in a rain cape with the flask in his pocket, and stood beside her until she took her hands from the wall.

**Halvard Roos**  
I can take it from here.

**Illuminara**  
Write it down.

**Halvard Roos**  
I already have. Nineteen hours, in a separate column. You are still not in my safety case.
She sat on the gallery floor. She could not feel her hands, and would not for six hours. Halvard unscrewed the flask and held it out, and she took it with both wrists.

scenes.title: The Seat
paragraphs: *Harrow Gorge Hearing Hall · Day Twelve, 10:00*
The witnesses had travelled through the night from three countries. They took the chair in turn. First, an old man lowered himself with one hand on the rush seat as if it might not hold.
Their engineers had read the bench survey, challenged two ledger rows and accepted the written rulings.

**Tomasz Brandl**  
Pell vetoes the right-bank route. We will not be under the dump. I carry Pell's register, not Quill's; the next witness carries theirs. We do not choose the left bank. That is the valley's land and choice.

**Savitri Moyo**  
At four this morning, thirty-eight of fifty-one landholding households chose the left bank with full-value purchase and the levy. Nine refused. Four abstained. I voted no. I carry the result because it is ours, not because it is mine.

**Bukola Ferreira**  
My city paid eleven rationing days. I put the levy on today's council docket. I do not cast the valley's vote.

**Adaeze**  
Then the record will show two decisions made by the people they bind, and none by anyone else.

Rule Four had stood amended since Day Two; today was its first use. Two disputed rows were settled before the storm, and Halvard's emergency log chose no route. By noon the cofferdam stood and excavation was within a day of schedule.
The Valley Courier called Adaeze a sentimentalist. The newsletter of the Lisk camp called her a bureaucrat. She read both and had them filed.
Illuminara waited at the door, her hands wrapped in gauze because Halvard had insisted.

**Adaeze**  
Nara. You are late.

**Illuminara**  
I was holding up your dam.

**Adaeze**  
I know. I read the log. And the fourth column.

Her mother crossed the hall, took the gauzed hands in both of hers, and looked at them for a moment without saying whether she thought the cost had been fair. Then she let go and went to find the carpenter. The chair, she had decided, would be fixed to the floor. The ledger would remain loose enough to turn.

critic_line: A dam that cannot wait and a village that cannot vote are reconciled by a ledger of what can still be undone, a challenge column nobody asked for, and nineteen hours of one woman's hands on a wall.

literary_score.method: Independent GPT 7D SA1 and Claude PEC-6 final scores; equal 50/50 model weight.
shared_strengths: The three-column ledger turns urgency, reversibility and representation into a precise procedure that can be challenged and audited.
Adaeze and the displaced communities retain decisive authority while Illuminara contributes engineering analysis without substituting her judgment for theirs.
shared_reservations: Several secondary characters remain sharply drawn institutional positions rather than fully dimensional people.
The compressed twelve-day process makes cross-border authorization and political acceptance feel somewhat cleaner than they would be in practice.

translation_sl.title: ADAEZE IN PRAZEN STOL
translation_sl.deck: Jez je treba začeti graditi pred deževjem, ljudje, katerih zemljo bo pokopal, pa nimajo glasu. Adaeze vodi zaslišanje; Illuminara ima dvanajst dni, da najde mejo med tem, kar ne more čakati, in tem, česar ni mogoče razveljaviti.
translation_sl.shape: Šest prizorov v dvanajstih dneh: zaslišanje s praznim stolom, zavrnitev med materjo in hčerjo, noč razčlenjevanja enega urnika v tri stolpce, glasovanje v treh državah, zgodnja nevihta v galeriji jezu in sedež, ki ni več prazen.

scenes.title: Postavka nič
paragraphs: *Dvorana za zaslišanja Harrow Gorge · prvi dan, 09:10*

Stol ob vznožju mize je bil prazen namenoma. Ogrodje iz jesena, sedež iz ločja, brez tablice z imenom. Adaeze ga je dala prinesti, preden so odprli vrata, zapisnikar pa ga je v zapisnik vnesel kot postavko nič.

Sedem vasi je stalo pod starim jezom do ukaza za evakuacijo pred enajstimi leti. Z ukazom so jih tudi razpustili. Njihovo zemljo so izbrisali iz registra, z njo pa njihove svete, in po Pravilu štiri so o jezu, ki naj bi ga zdaj zgradili čez njihove grobove, lahko glasovale samo skupnosti, ki so živele na kartiranem ozemlju.

**Halvard Roos**  
Galerija levega opornika pušča dva cela dve litra na sekundo. Moj prag je šest. Tej dvorani ne bom rekel, da je stari jez varen, in ne bom ji rekel, da novi lahko počaka na boljše zaslišanje.

**Bukola Ferreira**  
Šeststo tisoč ljudi pije iz te reke in deževje pride čez devetnajst dni. Vsaka ura, porabljena za duhove, je ura, odvzeta njim.
Adaeze ni dvignila pogleda s papirjev. Zaslišanja v porečju je vodila dvajset let in se naučila, da prostor najhitreje izgubiš, če odgovoriš na njegovo prvo žalitev.

**Adaeze**  
Duhovi imajo imena, svetnica. Zapisnikar jih bo prebral na koncu vsake seje, dokler se pravilo ne spremeni. Priča štiri, lahko začnete.
Illuminara je eno uro sedela pri stranski mizi in nihče je ni nagovoril drugače. Takšen je bil dogovor. Njena mati ga je sklenila v avtomobilu, v štirih stavkih, in je ni vprašala, ali ji ustreza.

**Illuminara**  
Za iztok prelivnega kanala sta izvedljivi dve trasi. Trasa po desnem bregu je ravnejša in cenejša, iztok in končno odlagališče izkopa pa vodi čez Pellove terase. Trasa po levem bregu vzame tristo deset hektarjev namakanih polj v Weirski dolini in stane devet odstotkov več. Obe sta varni. Nobena ni neškodljiva.

**Halvard Roos**  
Izvajalec pravi, da je treba traso določiti danes. Transportna cesta, izkop in zagatni jez so ena veriga.

**Illuminara**  
Tako pravi urnik. Nisem še preverila, ali tako pravi tudi skala.
Ob dolgi mizi je prazen stol držal okensko svetlobo. Nihče ni sedel na njem. Nihče ga tudi ni pogledal, in prav zato je vedela, da ga vsi štejejo.

scenes.title: Pravilo štiri
paragraphs: *Pisarna predsedujoče, dvorana za zaslišanja Harrow Gorge · prvi dan, 12:40*
Adaeze je zaprla vrata in snela očala, edino znamenje, ki ga je pokazala o tem, kako je minilo dopoldne.

**Illuminara**  
Prebrala sem vse štiri tisoč peticij iz treh držav. Z nekajodstotno natančnostjo lahko modeliram, kaj bi izbrala vsaka vas, in to vložim kot zapečateno ugotovitev. Potem stol ni prazen.

**Adaeze**  
Še enkrat povej drugi del, počasi.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bi glasovala namesto njih. Zaslišanju bi povedala, kaj bi najverjetneje rekli.

**Adaeze**  
Nara.
Izgovorila je kakor takrat, ko je bila njena hči stara štiriindvajset let in nova na sodiščih: ne kot grajo, temveč kot dlan, položeno plosko na mizo.

**Adaeze**  
Naučila si me prvega pravila svoje nekdanje obrti. Tolmačka prenese, kar govorec pove. Tega ne izboljšuje in ne dopolnjuje, ko govorca ni.

**Illuminara**  
Niso odsotni po lastni izbiri.

**Adaeze**  
Prav zato jih ne smeš nadomestiti. Bila bi tretje telo, ki bi odločilo namesto njih, tokrat prijazno. Takšno prijaznost sem že pokopala.
*Prav ima. Model bi bil natančen, pa bi bil še vedno kraja.*

**Illuminara**  
Kaj potem hočeš od mene?

**Adaeze**  
Stol ima veto in nima glasu. Ustavi lahko tisto, česar ni mogoče razveljaviti, ne more pa ničesar začeti. Prazen ostane, dokler pogrebna društva ne izberejo prič, ki bodo sedele na njem, za to pa bodo potrebovala dvanajst dni, ker živijo v treh državah in ne zaupajo nikomur. Dvorana me bo vprašala, koliko stane teh dvanajst dni. To mi moraš povedati. Ne, kaj hočejo vasi. Katere odločitve o jezu ostanejo odprte, če počakamo, in katere se za vedno zaprejo.

**Illuminara**  
To je inženirsko vprašanje.

**Adaeze**  
Edino takšno lahko odnesem svetnici Ferreira.
V stavbo je vstopila, da bi materi ponudila odgovor. Odšla je z vprašanjem in to je bilo boljše od obeh.

scenes.title: Veriga
paragraphs: *Pisarna izvajalca, gradbišče Harrow Gorge · prvi dan, 23:50*
Urnik Rute Kasprzak je obsegal štiristo dvanajst dejavnosti; Illuminara jih je do desete ure prebrala vse. Spraševala je, katere naloge so nujne. Adaeze je vprašala, katere je mogoče razveljaviti.

Vsako vrstico je označila s tremi vprašanji. Ali premakne skalo? Pokoplje zemljo? Zgradi nekaj, kar mora stati na končni izbiri? Tretje vprašanje je prestalo enaintrideset dejavnosti. Devet jih je zadevalo eno ali drugo traso. Preostale so tvorile eno verigo, ker je bilo tako najceneje odvažati.

**Ruta Kasprzak**  
Vrstica sto štiriinosemdeset. Ploščad betonarne. Dali ste jo v srednji stolpec, razveljavljivo za določeno ceno.

**Illuminara**  
Ploščo je mogoče razbiti.

**Ruta Kasprzak**  
Štirideset sidrnih pilotov seka traso transportne ceste po desnem bregu. Razbijte ploščo, pa piloti ostanejo pod cesto tiste trase, ki izgubi. Če jih izvlečem, izgubim dva dni in devetsto tisoč.
Illuminara je vrstico premaknila v tretji stolpec. Devet jih je postalo deset.

**Illuminara**  
Potem brez pilotov, dokler trasa ni izbrana. Mobilno betonarno postavite na gramozno blazino. Proizvodnji betona dodajte dva dni, devetsto tisoč pa v knjigo stroškov zaslišanja.

**Ruta Kasprzak**  
Hitro popustite za nekoga, ki je prebral vseh štiristo dvanajst.

**Illuminara**  
Knjiga je uporabna le, če jo lahko spremeni človek, ki dokaže, da se motim.
Ruta je s topim nohtom potrkala po naslovu stolpca. Illuminara je ob vsako razvrstitev dodala prazno polje: izpodbijalec, dokaz, čas vložitve. Tega stolpca ni zahteval nihče.

**Ruta Kasprzak**  
Še vedno hočete, da izkop pretovarjam dvakrat.

**Illuminara**  
Prvih dvesto dvainšestdeset tisoč kubičnih metrov je treba izkopati pred deževjem ne glede na zmagovalno traso. Zagatni jez, preusmeritveni predor in sidranje opornika ne zadevajo ne teras ne polj. Samo končno odlagališče in transportna cesta čez terase. Skalo namesto tega odpeljite na polico starega kamnoloma in pokopano ne bo nič, česar se ne bi dalo znova izkopati.

**Ruta Kasprzak**  
Po marčevski meritvi polica sprejme tristo tisoč. Od takrat razstreljujemo ob njej.

**Illuminara**  
Potem jo ob zori znova izmerimo.
Halvard Roos je opolnoči vstopil s termovko in brez vsakršnega namena, da bi se strinjal.

**Halvard Roos**  
Zaradi pravne fikcije hočete zamudo v mojem varnostnem primeru.

**Illuminara**  
V njem hočem strošek, ne zamude. Začasni prevoz po kamnolomski poti je počasnejši: devet dni nadur, milijon devetsto tisoč, enajst dni izvajalčeve rezerve. Cenejše poti nisem našla in ne trdim, da je brezplačna.

**Halvard Roos**  
Kaj pa, če deževje pride zgodaj? Jaz imam galerijo in prag. Vi imate preglednico.

**Illuminara**  
Če galerija preseže vaš prag, lahko približno trideset ur nosim strižne sile levega opornika. Ne dvanajst dni. Trideset ur, potem odpovem. Preostalo mora opraviti znižanje gladine: od jutri tri cele ena metra, kar pomeni, da bo mesto od jutri racioniralo vodo.

**Halvard Roos**  
Potem vas ni v mojem varnostnem primeru.

**Illuminara**  
Nisem prosila, da bi bila. Zapišite ločeno.

Ob zori je ponovna meritev pokazala dvesto devetinosemdeset tisoč kubičnih metrov, kar je pomenilo sedemindvajset tisoč nad ciljem izkopa, tri tisoč manj od Halvardove najmanjše rezerve. Ruta je za zadnje tri tisoč najela železniško skladišče za dodatnih sto osemdeset tisoč. Halvard je obe številki prebral dvakrat in ju z lastno roko vpisal v dnevnik.

scenes.title: Tri države
paragraphs: *Dvorana za zaslišanja Harrow Gorge, tri videopovezave · drugi dan, 10:00*

Povezave so zaživele: cerkvena dvorana v Corvanu, šolska telovadnica v Tessalyju, ladijska pisarna v Lisku. Enajst let so njihova pogrebna društva hranila registre sedmih vasi in pošiljala denar domov za pogrebe, kadar doma, kamor bi se lahko vrnili, ni bilo več.
Adaeze je prebrala predlog: prazen stol, veto nad nepovratnim delom, brez pritrdilnega glasu, dvanajstdnevni rok in Illuminarina knjiga po posameznih vrsticah.

**Bukola Ferreira**  
S tem tujcem dajemo veto nad vodo mojih volivcev. Čigavo vodo pijejo te priče?

**Adaeze**  
Ne vaše. Veto se nanaša samo na tretji stolpec. Racioniranje, zagatni jez in temeljenje se nadaljujejo.

**Mirela Haddad iz Corvana**  
Kdo pa ima v lasti tretji stolpec? Priča štiri? Vaš varnostni organ?
Illuminara je obrnila knjigo, da so vse tri kamere videle prazno polje ob vsaki vrstici.

**Illuminara**  
Varnostni organ razvrsti prvi. Inženir predsedujoče lahko vrstico izpodbija v štiriindvajsetih urah. Dokler ni obrazložene odločitve, velja bolj nepovratna razlaga. Ruta je našla vrstico, ki je dokazala, da izpodbijanje sodi sem.

**Mirela Haddad iz Corvana**  
Potem naš inženir, ki ga plača zaslišanje, prebere vaše številke in izmeri polico.

**Halvard Roos**  
Če galerija doseže prag, medtem ko je vrstica sporna, zaščitno delo ne more čakati.

**Illuminara**  
Samo delo, nujno za znižanje meritve pod prag, zapisano po urah in pregledano naslednji dan. Izjema ne sme izbrati trase.

**Savitri Moyo iz Weirske doline**  
Enaki pogoji za nas. Tukaj nihče ne sprejema levega brega v imenu doline. Sestanemo se enajsti dan; zapišite nestrinjanje.

**Bukola Ferreira**  
Po enem letu vrnite delovanje pravila na javno zaslišanje. Zagovarjam lahko omejeno zamudo, ne pa izmišljene izbire doline.

**Adaeze**  
Oba pogoja vnesite v predlog.

**Mirela Haddad iz Corvana**  
Priča štiri. Katera trasa pokoplje Pellove terase?

**Illuminara**  
Trasa po desnem bregu prekrije spodnje tri Pellove terase. Zaradi tega bi izbrala levo, vendar ta vzame polja ljudi na tem zaslišanju. Teh izgub ne bom tehtala.

**Bukola Ferreira**  
Glasujem za, z enoletnim pregledom. Glas doline ostaja njen.
Glasovanje se je končalo s šest proti tri. Pravilo štiri je začelo veljati opoldne. Adaeze, ki ni glasovala, je v zapisnik vpisala svoje avtorstvo in vsakršno krivdo.

scenes.title: Trideset ur
paragraphs: *Galerija levega opornika, stari jez Harrow Gorge · enajsti dan, 02:40*

Nevihta je prišla devet dni prezgodaj: sto štirideset milimetrov v devetih urah. Znižanje gladine je prineslo tri metre prostega roba in mesto stalo enajst dni racioniranja, toda nenaden dvig je skozi znano razpoko v levem oporniku potisnil tlak zbiralnika hitreje, kot so ga odtoki zmogli odvajati. Od dvesto dvainšestdeset tisoč kubičnih metrov, ki bi jih morali izkopati pred pričakovanim deževjem, jih je dvesto sedeminštirideset tisoč ležalo na polici kamnoloma. Preostalih petnajst tisoč je bilo še vedno skala v rezu ob reki; nevihta je prišla pred njihovo izmeno izkopa.
Ob 02:40 je odtok v galeriji kazal šest celih ena litra na sekundo.

**Halvard Roos po radijski zvezi**  
Preseglo je prag. Illuminara. Zdaj.

Vstopila je do tretje razpoke. Beton se je hladno potil. Obe dlani je položila na steno, našla ravnino, po kateri je opornik hotel zdrsniti, in začela nositi tisto, česar skala ni več nosila. Ni bilo kakor dvigovanje. Bilo je kakor stati v reki, ki želi, da stopiš vstran.
Rekla mu je trideset ur. Ni pogledala na uro.

**Halvard Roos po radijski zvezi**  
Pet celih štiri. Pada. Nadaljujte.
*Ne za vedno. Samo dokler znižanje gladine ne postane močnejša stvar.*

V devetnajsti uri je dotok v zbiralnik prešel svoj vrh. Ker je dež že ponehal, zbiralnik pa je bil tri metre nižji, kot bi bil sicer, so odtoki znova prevzeli obremenitev. Meritev je padla na dve celi devet in tam obstala. Halvard je sam prišel v galerijo, v dežnem ogrinjalu in s termovko v žepu, ter stal ob njej, dokler ni odmaknila rok s stene.

**Halvard Roos**  
Od tod lahko prevzamem.

**Illuminara**  
Zapišite.

**Halvard Roos**  
Sem že. Devetnajst ur, v ločenem stolpcu. Še vedno vas ni v mojem varnostnem primeru.
Sedla je na tla galerije. Rok ni čutila in jih še šest ur ne bo. Halvard je odvil termovko in ji jo ponudil, ona pa jo je prijela z obema zapestjema.

scenes.title: Sedež
paragraphs: *Dvorana za zaslišanja Harrow Gorge · dvanajsti dan, 10:00*
Priče so vso noč potovale iz treh držav. Na stol so sedle po vrsti. Najprej se je nanj spustil starec z eno roko na sedežu iz ločja, kakor da ta morda ne bo zdržal.
Njihovi inženirji so prebrali meritev police, izpodbijali dve vrstici knjige in sprejeli pisni odločitvi.

**Tomasz Brandl**  
Pell vlaga veto na traso po desnem bregu. Ne bomo pod odlagališčem. Nosim Pellov register, ne Quillovega; naslednja priča nosi njihovega. Levega brega ne izbiramo. To je zemlja in izbira doline.

**Savitri Moyo**  
Ob štirih zjutraj je osemintrideset od enainpetdesetih gospodinjstev z zemljišči izbralo levi breg s plačilom polne vrednosti in dajatvijo. Devet jih je zavrnilo. Štiri so se vzdržala. Glasovala sem proti. Izid prinašam, ker je naš, ne zato, ker je moj.

**Bukola Ferreira**  
Moje mesto je plačalo enajst dni racioniranja. Dajatev uvrščam na današnji dnevni red sveta. Ne oddajam glasu doline.

**Adaeze**  
Potem bo zapisnik pokazal dve odločitvi, ki so ju sprejeli ljudje, katere zavezujeta, in nobene, ki bi jo sprejel kdo drug.

Pravilo štiri je bilo spremenjeno že od drugega dne; danes so ga uporabili prvič. Dve sporni vrstici sta bili rešeni pred nevihto, Halvardov nujni dnevnik pa ni izbral nobene trase. Opoldne je zagatni jez stal in izkop je za urnikom zaostajal manj kot dan.
Valley Courier je Adaeze označil za sentimentalistko. Glasilo taborišča Lisk jo je označilo za birokratko. Prebrala je oboje in naročila, naj vložijo oba zapisa.
Illuminara je čakala pri vratih, z rokami, povitimi v gazo, ker je Halvard vztrajal.

**Adaeze**  
Nara. Zamujaš.

**Illuminara**  
Držala sem pokonci tvoj jez.

**Adaeze**  
Vem. Prebrala sem dnevnik. In četrti stolpec.

Njena mati je prečkala dvorano, vzela poviti roki v svoji dlani in ju nekaj časa gledala, ne da bi povedala, ali se ji je zdela cena pravična. Potem ju je izpustila in odšla poiskat mizarja. Odločila se je, da bo stol pritrjen na tla. Knjiga bo ostala dovolj prosta, da jo bo mogoče obrniti.

translation_sl.critic_line: Jez, ki ne more čakati, in vas, ki ne more glasovati, spravi knjiga tega, kar je še mogoče razveljaviti, stolpec za ugovore, ki ga ni zahteval nihče, ter devetnajst ur rok ene ženske na steni.
